title: 11 Facts About Space That Should Be Illegal to Know

scenes.voiceover: Somewhere out there... a black hole is eating an entire Sun every single day. Not metaphorically. Literally. And it's not even the most disturbing thing I'm going to show you tonight.
scenes.mainText: A BLACK HOLE EATS A SUN A DAY

scenes.voiceover: Its name is J0529 dash 4351. Seventeen billion times the mass of our Sun... and its accretion disc alone is seven light-years wide. Fifteen thousand times the distance from our Sun to Neptune.
scenes.mainText: 1 SUN, EVERY DAY, FOREVER

stat.label: SOLAR MASSES — THE BRIGHTEST OBJECT EVER FOUND

scenes.voiceover: But that's just something eating. Let me show you something dying — because in two thousand fifteen, we heard two black holes collide for the first time in human history.
scenes.mainText: THEN TWO OF THEM COLLIDED

scenes.voiceover: In a fraction of a second... they converted three entire Suns' worth of mass directly into pure energy. For that instant, it outshined every single star in the observable universe. Combined.
scenes.mainText: BRIGHTER THAN EVERY STAR COMBINED

scenes.voiceover: Now here's the one that keeps me up at night. If you watched a friend fall into a black hole... you would never actually see them cross the edge.
scenes.mainText: YOU WOULD NEVER SEE THEM CROSS

scenes.voiceover: To you, watching from outside... they freeze. They dim. They fade to black, forever, never quite disappearing. But to them? They feel nothing. They cross instantly, and keep falling.
scenes.mainText: THEY FREEZE FOREVER. THEY FEEL NOTHING.
scenes.kicker: TWO PEOPLE, TWO REALITIES, BOTH TRUE

scenes.voiceover: Let's come back to something warmer. The sunlight on your skin right now... it did not just arrive. It has been traveling since before humans existed.
scenes.mainText: THIS LIGHT IS OLDER THAN HUMANITY
scenes.kicker: THE LONGEST JOURNEY IN THE SOLAR SYSTEM

scenes.voiceover: Deep in the Sun's core, a photon is born... and it bounces, and bounces, and bounces off plasma so dense it takes up to one hundred seventy thousand years just to escape. Then eight minutes to reach you.
scenes.mainText: 170,000 YEARS TO ESCAPE THE SUN
scenes.kicker: THEN JUST 8 MINUTES TO REACH EARTH

scenes.voiceover: Now let's talk about the densest objects in the universe. You've heard the teaspoon fact. Forget it. Here's the one nobody tells you.
scenes.mainText: FORGET THE TEASPOON. THIS IS WEIRDER.

scenes.voiceover: A neutron star is more massive than our Sun, crushed into a city-sized sphere. And yet its tallest mountain... is less than one millimeter tall. Gravity there is so extreme, it flattens everything.
scenes.mainText: TALLEST MOUNTAIN: UNDER 1 MILLIMETER
scenes.kicker: ON AN OBJECT HEAVIER THAN THE SUN

scenes.voiceover: But mountains are the least scary thing about these objects. In two thousand four, one of them screamed — and Earth felt it, from clear across the galaxy.
scenes.mainText: EARTH FELT IT FROM ACROSS THE GALAXY

scenes.voiceover: A magnetar, fifty thousand light-years away, released more energy in two-tenths of a second than our Sun produces in over a hundred thousand years. It measurably disturbed our own atmosphere. From fifty thousand light-years.
scenes.mainText: 0.2 SECONDS = 100,000+ YEARS OF OUR SUN

scenes.voiceover: Let's move from the terrifying to the impossible. Somewhere in our galaxy, there is a dead star spinning faster than your mind can process.
scenes.mainText: A DEAD STAR, SPINNING IMPOSSIBLY FAST

scenes.voiceover: PSR J1748, minus 2446 A D, spins seven hundred sixteen times... every single second. Its surface is moving at nearly a quarter of the speed of light. Any faster, and it would tear itself apart.
scenes.mainText: 716 ROTATIONS. EVERY SECOND.
scenes.kicker: SURFACE SPEED: ~24% THE SPEED OF LIGHT

scenes.voiceover: Here's one hiding in your pocket right now. Every GPS satellite above you is deliberately built with a mistake — because Einstein demanded it.
scenes.mainText: YOUR PHONE IS BUILT ON A MISTAKE

scenes.voiceover: Its speed slows its clock by seven microseconds a day. Weaker gravity up there speeds it up by forty-five. Uncorrected, your location would drift by ten kilometers... every single day.
scenes.mainText: UNCORRECTED: 10 KM OF DRIFT, PER DAY
scenes.kicker: GRAVITY WINS BY 38 MICROSECONDS A DAY

scenes.voiceover: You'd think black holes last forever. They don't. But the number for how long they actually take... will break your sense of scale.
scenes.mainText: EVEN BLACK HOLES EVENTUALLY DIE

scenes.voiceover: A 2025 recalculation says a stellar black hole fully evaporates in ten, to the power of sixty-seven years. That's a one, followed by sixty-seven zeroes. The universe itself is only thirteen point eight billion years old.
scenes.mainText: 10 with 67 ZEROES — IN YEARS
scenes.kicker: THE UNIVERSE ISN'T EVEN 1% OF THE WAY THERE

stat.label: YEARS FOR A BLACK HOLE TO FULLY EVAPORATE

scenes.voiceover: And now, the one that actually changed how I see the night sky. Most of what you can see up there... you can never, ever visit.
scenes.mainText: YOU WILL NEVER REACH MOST OF THE SKY

scenes.voiceover: Ninety-four percent of the galaxies in our observable universe are already permanently unreachable. Space itself is expanding faster than light could ever cross it. Even if you left today, at light speed... you would never, ever arrive.
scenes.mainText: 94% OF THE UNIVERSE — GONE, FOREVER
scenes.kicker: EVEN AT THE SPEED OF LIGHT

stat.label: OF THE UNIVERSE YOU CAN NEVER REACH

scenes.voiceover: And here's the strangest part. The thing pushing all of that away — dark energy — might be weakening. If it is... the universe stops expanding. And starts, instead, to fall back in on itself.
scenes.mainText: "IT MIGHT ALL FALL BACK IN ON ITSELF"
scenes.kicker: DESI 2025 — AN UNRESOLVED DEBATE, NOT A FACT

scenes.voiceover: Nobody knows how this ends yet. Not really. That's the part that should terrify and delight you in equal measure. Subscribe to mindwired... because I'm not done looking.
scenes.mainText: SUBSCRIBE — I'M NOT DONE LOOKING
